activities.evidence: Slide 16: "Wk1: Arrive Ready inserts live; trust badges above fold; test-ride bookings open; press outreach. budget.evidence: Slide 17: "Total $21,000: media $8,000 [A4]; creators 8 x $800 [A6]; events 8 x $300 [A7]; inserts [A9]; tools [A10]; contingency [A11]" - 6 lines sum correctly to $21,000 with labeled assumption bases, funnel math (1.2M x 1.5% x 0.6% = ~108 orders x $950), profit-based ROI ~56%, breakeven ~66, and an honest conservative case (-$7K at 40% factor) plus margin sensitivity 25%->-14% / 40%->+95%. Weakness: conservative mitigation relies on '~$12K list value' for captures not yet built plus unquantified support savings, and W_FINANCE warning confirms the losing case is only partially addressed
budget.fix: Quantify the conservative-case offset (actual email/SMS revenue assumption, support-ticket cost per case from review data) or show a second scenario that stays profitable; tie each line item to a real quote/benchmark rather than self-labeled assumptions.

impact.evidence: Slide 18: "O3: 1-star review share recount - re-crawl Judge.me corpus bi-weekly, same keyword method" with per-objective tools (Shopify code + UTM, Klaviyo, event tally), targets (90 orders, 400 rides/800 captures, <50% share), leading/lagging indicators, and off-track triggers ('if wk3 rides <150, shift media to CA'). Baselines are thin for the new codes ('0 (new codes)') and order attribution lacks an incrementality control outside the test-ride program
impact.fix: Add a baseline period for order volume/review mix before launch and extend the control-group design to paid traffic so attributed orders are incremental, not just tagged.
